chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man commits adultery and is whipped, it is befitting for the Imam to exile him from the land in which he was whipped to another. Indeed, it is upon the Imam to remove him from the city in which he was whipped.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exiling an adulterer after whipping according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the judicial discretion of the Imam in enforcing *Tazir* (disciplinary punishment) by mandating exile from the specific locality of the offense to prevent recurrence and maintain social order. This ruling highlights the practical application of penal authority in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the fixed *Hadd* punishment of whipping and the variable administrative measure of banishment. It underscores the Imam's role in managing public morality through spatial separation of the offender from the community where the transgression occurred.
